reason: The text explicitly describes the establishment and enforcement of a strict hierarchical system in Egypt. Pharaoh appoints taskmasters over the Israelites (שָׂרֵי מִסִּים - 'officers of burdens') to afflict them systematically. The power structure is clearly delineated: Pharaoh issues commands, taskmasters enforce his will, and the Israelites are subjugated laborers. The text provides no criticism, discouragement, or devaluation of this hierarchy; rather, it depicts Pharaoh deliberately implementing stratification as a political strategy to control a populous minority. The hierarchy is presented as central to the narrative's concerns.
